title: Aston Villa ex-president of football operations Monchi close to Espanyol role
content:
Aston Villa’s former president of football operations Monchi is close to joining Espanyol.

Monchi, 57, departed Villa in September following the club’s disappointing start to the season and criticism over their transfer strategy.

Sources briefed on the situation, speaking on the condition of anonymity to protect relationships, indicated he is being lined up for a head of football role with Espanyol.

The potential move would see Monchi return to La Liga and his native Spain, having had two spells at Sevilla as the club’s sporting director either side of a stint at Roma (2017-2019).

Monchi joined Villa in 2023 and was a key figure in the club’s rise into the Champions League, alongside manager Unai Emery and director of football operations, Damian Vidagany. The Athletic reported Emery had the overarching say on signings, with Monchi’s remit being to facilitate the Villa manager’s wishes.

Roberto Olabe was appointed Monchi’s successor in September.

Villa endured a difficult start to the season, failing to win any of their opening five league matches and scoring just once, but have experienced an upturn in fortunes and are on course to qualify for the Champions League, in addition to reaching the Europa League semi-finals.

Emery’s side are fifth in the Premier League, six points above Bournemouth with three games remaining.

Monchi, a former goalkeeper, had a nine-year playing career with Sevilla before retiring in 1999.

Espanyol are 13th in La Liga, with the Barcelona-based club returning to the Spanish top flight in 2024.
